title: Bounded colimit apices and homotopy retracts are essentially small
statement: Use the universes, local smallness, essential smallness and $\beta$-small simplicial sets of [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category], and coherent diagrams, mapping spaces and colimits of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Let $\mathcal E$ be a locally small quasicategory. Let $\mathcal G\subseteq\mathcal E$ be an essentially small full subcategory and $\beta$ an infinite regular cardinal in the smaller universe. The full subcategory of objects equivalent to apices of existing colimiting cocones $q:K\to\mathcal G\hookrightarrow\mathcal E$, as $K$ ranges over all $\beta$-small simplicial sets, is essentially small. Also the full subcategory of objects $x$ admitting maps $i:x\to g$ and $r:g\to x$ for some $g\in\mathcal G$ with $r i$ in the same connected component of $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}(x,x)$ as $1_x$ is essentially small. No existence of the colimits or of splittings of arbitrary idempotents is assumed.

source.place: Proposition 5.4.1.7 and Proposition 5.4.1.2, printed pp. 419-423 (small object family plus local smallness); the bounded-diagram counting argument in Proposition 5.4.2.9, printed p. 426; the small retract-envelope argument in Lemma 5.4.2.4, printed pp. 424-425, and Section 5.1.4. The bounded-colimit and homotopy-retract variants are stated here as a general size-calculus consequence, not verbatim from one proposition. Read online, not archived under literature/. No Stacks tag supplies these coherent size assertions.
